Samir (Finance): Heads up — card network opened a dispute (fraud) against account ACME-967 for a bunch of low-value charges. System auto-put account on temporary hold. Need recommendations on evidence packet and whether we keep hold.

Priya (Billing): Seen it. Can you paste the txn ids? Are these new customers or existing?

Samir (Finance): New-ish. Small recurring micro-charges, likely card-testing. Here are the txns we pulled:
```
txn_9a1b: 2025-05-11T03:12:08Z amount $0.99 card ****4242 ip 18.203.12.5
txn_f3c4: 2025-05-11T03:15:42Z amount $1.99 card ****4242 ip 18.203.12.5
txn_b772: 2025-05-11T03:20:01Z amount $2.99 card ****4242 ip 3.10.45.9
chargeback_id: cb_20250511_8801
```

ChargebackBot: Automated note — evidence deadline 10 days from dispute open. Priority: high.

Liam (Support): @Samir do we have any successful delivery/usage logs tied to those sessions? Could be test attempts or legit infra usage.

Samir (Finance): We have API logs showing tokens consumed ~0–3 per request; user agent looks like curl. No authenticated account actions. Attached sample API header: `User-Agent: curl/7.83.1` and `Authorization: Bearer redacted`.

Eloise (Risk Ops): This smells like card testing. IPs are different but within AWS ranges. We should: 1) gather full network headers + reverse DNS, 2) include refund history (none), 3) provide user-agent, 4) include onboarding info (email used, any KYC). Also preserve raw logs for forensics.

Priya (Billing): I can prepare the txn receipts and a timeline. Question for Legal-Review — do we push for representment or accept the dispute? Representment requires proof of cardholder acceptance or merchant receipt. We only have minimal headers and no customer-provided order details.

Legal-Review: If card-testing, reps are low chance unless merchant can show signed auth or digital agreement. Still worth sending evidence: IPs, UA, onboarding email, timestamps, and note that these amounts were below $3 and match card-testing pattern. We'll draft language but set expectation: 30–40% success at best.

Samir (Finance): OK — plan: Priya assemble receipts + timeline; Eloise collect network headers and preserve logs; Liam flag account hold for 48 hours and escalate to Dedicated ops if they request capacity; Legal will draft evidence narrative. I'll compile and submit before deadline.

Priya (Billing): I'll attach the invoices and mark the transactions as disputed in the ledger. Also will submit internal memo for chargeback reserve adjustment.

Liam (Support): I'll message the customer support inbox template so CS can tell the customer their account is on hold pending fraud review. Sample blurb: "We've temporarily limited activity on your account while we investigate suspicious card activity. We will update within 48 hours."

Eloise (Risk Ops): Also recommend we run a fraud-screen on the saved payment method and block the BIN range if pattern repeats. Adding rule to watchlist: more than 3 micro-charges < $5 within 30 mins.

Samir (Finance): Approved. Everyone: upload docs to the chargeback folder and @Legal-Review once ready. I'll submit evidence packet and update this thread when done. :thumbsup:

ChargebackBot: Evidence packet submitted by Samir at 2025-05-11T18:02:25Z (submission_id: sub_20250511_9902)

Priya (Billing): Noted — reserved funds updated. Will monitor outcome.

Samir (Finance): Closing loop here once network reply from card network comes in. If representment fails, recommend full refund + remove hold but keep watchlist rule.

Legal-Review: I'll post final language used in representment to this thread after submission for record.

Liam (Support): Thanks all.
